'''Zabian Dowdell''' (born September 10, 1984) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Born in [[Pahokee, Florida]], he played basketball for [[Pahokee High School|his hometown's high school]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University|Virginia Tech]] [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Hokies]] from 2003 to 2007. In his senior season he was named in the First-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] and the ACC All-Defensive team. Following his graduation from college, Dowdell played professionally mainly in Europe, also having brief stints in the [[NBA]] and the [[NBA D-League]].

==Early life==
Dowdell attended [[Pahokee High School]], where he played [[Basketball#U.S. high school basketball|high school basketball]] and was first team all-state as a junior and senior.  In 2003, he was named [[The Palm Beach Post]] 6A-3A Player of the Year, Palm Beach Post Small School Player of the Year, and Florida [[Dairy Farmers of America|Dairy Farmers]] 3A Player of the Year.  As a senior, Dowdell averaged 23 points, eight [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] and seven [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game.

==College career==
Dowdell attended and played [[college basketball]] at [[Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University|Virginia Tech]] from 2003 to 2007.  A four-year starter, Dowdell and teammate [[Jamon Gordon]] were considered one of the best [[Basketball position#Backcourt (guards)|backcourt]] duos in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]].<ref>{{cite news | newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] | url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/01/12/AR2007011202200.html | title=They Have Each Other's Backs | access-date=2009-06-28 | first=Adam | last=Kilgore | date=2007-01-13}}</ref>  Dowdell is the seventh leading scorer (1,785) in Virginia Tech history, as well as fifth in assists (380), and third in steals (241).<ref>{{cite web | work=TechHoops.com | url=http://www.techhoops.com/hokie-career-recordsleaders/ | title=Hokie Career Records/Leaders | access-date=2009-07-04 | archive-date=July 20, 2009 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090720032830/http://techhoops.com/hokie-career-recordsleaders/ | url-status=dead }}</ref>  He was [[Seth Greenberg]]'s first signee at Virginia Tech.

Dowdell scored in double figures in his first 41 ACC regular season games.<ref>{{cite web | work=TechHoops.com | url=http://www.techhoops.com/zabian-dowdell/ | title=TechHoops – Zabian Dowdell | access-date=2009-06-28 | archive-date=May 30, 2007 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070530002139/http://www.techhoops.com/zabian-dowdell | url-status=dead }}</ref>  He was named [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] honorable mention twice, [[2006–07 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season#All-ACC Defensive team|All-ACC Defensive team]] twice, and [[All-America]]n honorable mention in 2006–07.  He was also named to the first team All-ACC during his senior season, becoming the first Hokie to do so.  His accomplishments at the university led to his induction into the Virginia Tech Sports Hall of Fame in 2017.

===Freshman season===
Dowdell made his first collegiate start on November 22, 2003, in the win over the [[University of New Hampshire]].  During the game, he scored 15 points, with five assists and three steals.<ref name=stats2004>[https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4327/type/college/year/2004/zabian-dowdell Zabian Dowdell Game By Game Stats and Performance – Virginia Tech – ESPN (2003–2004 Regular Season Game Log)]</ref> He scored a season-high 20 points during a win against [[West Virginia University]].<ref name=stats2004/> At the end of the regular season, Dowdell played in two games of the [[2004 Big East men's basketball tournament|2004 Big East tournament]], during which he scored 21 points, and had eight assists and seven steals.<ref name=stats2004/> Dowdell started 28 games and scored in double figures 15 times.<ref name=stats2004/> He was second on the team in assists and scoring.

===Sophomore season===
On February 2, 2005, Dowdell tied a career-high with five three-pointers and scored a season-high 23 points in a win over the [[University of Miami]] in front of a large crowd from his hometown of [[Pahokee, Florida]].  On February 17, 2005, he hit the game-winning three-pointer and scored 11 points and two assists in the win over seventh-ranked [[Duke University]] in [[Cassell Coliseum]], one of the most famous victories in [[Cassell Coliseum#Major games|Virginia Tech basketball history]].  After the regular season,  Dowdell totaled 24 points, four rebounds and three assists in two games of the [[2005 National Invitation Tournament]], including 16 points in a first-round win over [[Temple University]].<ref name=stats2005>[https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4327/type/college/year/2005/zabian-dowdell Zabian Dowdell Game By Game Stats and Performance – Virginia Tech – ESPN (2004–2005 Regular Season Game Log)]</ref> The tournament was Virginia Tech's first postseason appearance in nine years and their first [[National Invitation Tournament]] appearance in a decade.<ref>{{cite web | work=[[ESPN|ESPN.com]] | url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=250740259 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121102220930/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=250740259 | url-status=dead | archive-date=November 2, 2012 | title=Chaney returns after five-game suspension | access-date=2009-07-06}}</ref>

Dowdell started 29 games and scored in double figures 26 times.<ref name=stats2005/>  He averaged 14.4 points and had four games of 20 or more points.  He was 16th in scoring in the ACC (tenth in league games), 11th in steals, and third in three-point field goal percentage.  He was named an All-ACC honorable mention and first-team All-State by the Virginia Sports Information Directors (VaSID) and the ''[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]]''.

===Junior season===
On December 7, 2005, Dowdell scored a then career-high 25 points against [[North Carolina Agricultural and Technical State University|North Carolina A&T State University]],<ref name=NCAT>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130124172936/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=253410259|title=North Carolina A&T Aggies vs. Virginia Tech Hokies – Recap – December 07, 2005 – ESPN}}</ref> as well as career highs in field goals made (nine), three-point field goals made (seven; tying a school record<ref name=NCAT/>) and three-point field goals attempted (12).  On January 21, 2006, he scored 21 points and had six assists against the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]].<ref name=stats2006>[https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4327/type/college/year/2006/zabian-dowdell Zabian Dowdell Game By Game Stats and Performance – Virginia Tech – ESPN (2005–2006 Regular Season Game Log)]</ref> During the game, he hit eight of his final 12 shots<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/playbyplay?gameId=260210120 Virginia Tech Hokies vs. Maryland Terrapins – Play by Play – January 21, 2006 – ESPN]</ref> and scored his 1,000th career point.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120709020509/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=260210120|title=Virginia Tech Hokies vs. Maryland Terrapins – Recap – January 21, 2006 – ESPN}}</ref>  After the regular season, he scored 15 points against the [[University of Virginia]] in the [[2006 ACC men's basketball tournament|2006 ACC tournament]].<ref name=stats2006/> He also had four assists and four steals.<ref name=stats2006/>

Dowdell led the Hokies in scoring (15.3 ppg), steals (70) and minutes played.  He started 28 of 30 games and scored in double figures 28 times.<ref name=stats2006/> He was named an All-ACC Honorable mention for the second consecutive season and second-team All-State by the ''Richmond Times-Dispatch''.  Dowdell was also named to the ACC All-Defensive team.

===Senior season===
On January 6, 2007, Dowdell scored 20 points and had five steals in an overtime win against fifth-ranked [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke University]] in [[Cameron Indoor Stadium]], the Hokies first win at that arena.<ref>{{cite web | work=TechSideline.com | url=http://www.techsideline.com/news_archive/showArticle-2591.php | title=Sweet Revenge: Hokies Beat #5 Duke 69–67 in Overtime  | access-date=2010-05-30}}</ref>  On January 13, 2007, he scored 23 points and had four steals in a win over the first-ranked [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|University of North Carolina]] in [[Cassell Coliseum]],<ref>{{cite news | work=[[USA Today]] | url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/games/2007-01-13-vatech-unc_x.htm?POE=SPOISVA | title=Virginia Tech makes North Carolina's stay at No. 1 short with 94–88 upset | access-date=2009-06-28 | date=2007-01-13}}</ref> ending North Carolina's 12-game winning streak.<ref>{{cite web | work=SportsNetwork | url=http://www.wisn.com/sports/10741727/detail.html | title=Va. Tech Upsets No. 1 UNC | access-date=2009-06-28}}</ref>  On February 13, 2007, Dowdell scored a career-high 33 points in an 81–80 overtime win again against fourth-ranked North Carolina in the [[Dean Smith Center]],<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120707204817/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=270440153|title=Virginia Tech Hokies vs. North Carolina Tar Heels – Recap – February 13, 2007 – ESPN}}</ref> completing the sweep.  He scored six of those points in overtime, and made 17 of 19 free throws, including the game-winning points with a pair of foul shots with 1 minute 27 seconds remaining.<ref>{{cite news | newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] | url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/02/13/AR2007021301581.html | title=Virginia Tech Sweeps Tar Heels | access-date=2009-06-28 | first=Adam | last=Kilgore | date=2007-02-14}}</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/playbyplay?gameId=270440153 Virginia Tech Hokies vs. North Carolina Tar Heels – Play by Play – February 13, 2007 – ESPN]</ref> After the regular season, he scored 28 points, had six assists, and had five steals in two games of the [[2007 ACC men's basketball tournament|2007 ACC tournament]].<ref name=stats2007>[https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4327/type/college/year/2007/zabian-dowdell Zabian Dowdell Game By Game Stats and Performance – Virginia Tech – ESPN (2006–2007 Regular Season Game Log)]</ref>  Dowdell then scored 15 points in two games of the [[2007 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2007 NCAA tournament]].<ref name=stats2007/>  The first-round game, a win against the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign|University of Illinois]], was the Hokies' first NCAA Tournament victory since the [[1996 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|1996 NCAA tournament]].

Dowdell started in 33 games, scored in double figures 29 times, led the Hokies in scoring (17.4 ppg), and finished second in steals (71) and assists (106).  He was second in the ACC in steals per game (2.1) and fifth in free three percentage (80.6).  Dowdell was named the [[2006-07 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season#Players of the week|ACC Player of the Week]] twice during the season.  He also earned [[2006–07 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season#All-Atlantic Coast Conference|All-ACC first team]] honors (becoming the first Hokie to do so), and was named to the [[2006-07 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season#All-ACC Defensive team|All-ACC Defensive team]].

==Professional career==

===NBA draft===
Before the [[NBA draft]], Dowdell played with the Tidewater Sealants in the [[Portsmouth Invitational Tournament]], which is the oldest amateur [[basketball]] tournament and is the only [[postseason]] camp conducted for the top [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] seniors.<ref name=pit>{{cite web | work=[[National Basketball Association|NBA.com]] | url=http://www.nba.com/features/pit_070405.html | title=Keeping 'Score' at the PIT | access-date=2009-07-03}}</ref>  Dowdell and the Sealants lost in the opening round against Holiday Inn Portsmouth, 110–71, and Dowdell led the Sealants in scoring with 22 points.<ref name=pit />  Dowdell then went undrafted in the [[2007 NBA draft]].  He was projected to go as high as #28 in the first round to the [[San Antonio Spurs]], and many other [[mock draft]]s had him going in the second round.<ref>{{cite web | work=TechSideline.com | url=http://www.techsideline.com/news_archive/showArticle-2951.php | title=Despite High Marks, Dowdell Not Drafted  | access-date=2009-07-03}}</ref>

===SLUC Nancy===
After going undrafted in the [[2007 NBA draft]], Dowdell played for the [[NBA]]'s [[Seattle SuperSonics]] in the 2007 [[NBA Summer League]] at the [[Thomas & Mack Center]] and the [[Cox Pavilion]] in [[Las Vegas Valley|Las Vegas]], Nevada from July 6 to the 15.

He then signed a contract with the French team [[SLUC Nancy]] of the [[LNB Pro A|French League]]. On June 15, 2008, Dowdell and SLUC Nancy won the [[Ligue Nationale de Basketball#LNB champions|LNB Championship game]] against defending champion [[Chorale Roanne Basket]], 84–53. He played for 14 minutes and scored two points.<ref>{{cite web|work=[[Ligue Nationale de Basketball]]|url=http://www.lnb.fr/index.php?pid=6&game=3369|title=2007–08 LNB Championship Results|access-date=2009-06-29}}</ref>

Dowdell and SLUC Nancy also played in the [[ULEB Cup 2007-08|2007–08]] [[ULEB Eurocup|ULEB Cup]] (now known as the ULEB Eurocup), a competition that included 54 teams, initially divided in nine groups of six teams. SLUC Nancy, who played in [[ULEB Cup 2007-08 Regular Season Group D|Group D]], was eliminated during the [[Round-robin tournament|round-robin group stage]] (regular season) and did not participate in the [[ULEB Cup 2007-08 Knockout Stage|knockout stage]] or the [[ULEB Cup 2007-08 Final Eight|playoffs]]. Dowdell played in all ten regular season games and had 112 points, 32 assists, 28 rebounds and 12 steals.<ref>{{cite web | work=DraftExpress.com | url=http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Zabian-Dowdell-472/stats/ | title=Draft Express profile – Zabian Dowdell | access-date=2009-06-29 | archive-date=March 9, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120309171345/http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Zabian-Dowdell-472/stats/ | url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Pallacanestro Casale===
Dowdell signed with [[A.S. Junior Pallacanestro Casale]] (known as Fastweb Casale) in the [[LegADue]], the second-highest division of professional basketball in Italy. He played in all 30 regular season games and averaged 20.7 points per game. On November 2, 2008, he scored a season-high 36 points in a win against [[Pallacanestro Reggiana|Trenkwalder Reggio Emilia]], 91–87.<ref name=eurobasketprofile>{{cite web | work=EuroBasket.com | url=http://www.eurobasket.com/player.asp?Cntry=ITA&PlayerID=58515 | title=Zabian Dowdell Basketball Player Profile | access-date=2009-07-03}}</ref> In the quarterfinals of the postseason, Fastweb Casale won three straight games against [[Basket Rimini Crabs|Coopsette Rimini]] to sweep the series and advance.<ref name=eurobasketfastweb>{{cite web | work=EuroBasket.com | url=http://www.eurobasket.com/team.asp?Cntry=ITALY&Team=4159&Page=2 | title=Fastweb Junior Casale Monferrato basketball | access-date=2009-07-03}}</ref> In the three games, Dowdell had 39 points, 11 assists, 12 rebounds, and five steals.<ref name=eurobasketprofile />  Fastweb Casale then lost the semi-final series, 3–2, against [[Gruppo Triboldi Basket|Vanoli Soresina]] and were eliminated.<ref name=eurobasketfastweb /> In that series, Dowdell had 91 points, 15 assists, 20 rebounds, and 12 steals.<ref name=eurobasketprofile />

===NBA D-League and Spanish clubs===
Dowdell played for the [[Phoenix Suns]] in the NBA Summer League in 2010.<ref>http://www.ridiculousupside.com/2010/6/28/1540775/nba-summer-league-rosters-vegas {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151021193042/http://www.ridiculousupside.com/2010/6/28/1540775/nba-summer-league-rosters-vegas |date=October 21, 2015 }} NBA Summer League Rosters – Vegas</ref> His play allowed him to sign up for their training camp with undrafted rookie ex-[[Northeastern University|Northeastern]] [[Northeastern Huskies men's basketball|Husky]] [[Matt Janning]] and veteran NBA point guard [[Chucky Atkins]].

Following the NBA Summer League, he signed a deal with the [[Tulsa 66ers]], one of the [[NBA Development League]] teams. After four months, he decided to move on, accepting an offer of the Spanish club [[Unicaja Málaga]].

In 2012, he signed with [[CB Gran Canaria|Gran Canaria]].<ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/219309/Zabian_Dowdell_Agrees_To_Terms_With_Gran_Canaria Zabian Dowdell Agrees To Terms With Gran Canaria]</ref> 
 
===Phoenix Suns===
On January 9, 2011, the Suns signed Dowdell to a ten-day contract.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/basketball/nba/wires/01/09/2030.ap.bkn.suns.signing.1st.ld.writethru.0148/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103194000/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/basketball/nba/wires/01/09/2030.ap.bkn.suns.signing.1st.ld.writethru.0148/ | url-status=dead | archive-date=November 3, 2012 | work=CNN | title=Suns sign Zabian Dodwell to 10-day contract | date=2011-01-09}}</ref>  He signed a second ten-day contract on January 27, 2011.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/dowdell_10day_110127.html|title=Suns Sign Dowdell to Another 10-Day Contract|website=[[NBA.com]] }}</ref> Dowdell was featured in the January 31, 2011 issue of [[Sports Illustrated]] in an article about NBA players with ten-day contracts. On February 7, 2011, the Suns signed Dowdell through the remainder of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/dowdell_signed_110207.html|title = Suns Sign Dowdell for Remainder of Season| website=[[NBA.com]] }}</ref> On December 13, the Suns announced that they had waived Dowdell and replaced him with [[Ronnie Price]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.azcentral.com/sports/suns/articles/2011/12/13/20111213phoenix-suns-waive-zabian-dowdell.html|title = Phoenix Suns waive backup Zabian Dowdell}}</ref> On January 18, 2012, Dowdell signed a contract with [[Efes Pilsen S.K.|Anadolu Efes Pilsen]]. However, due to a failed physical, he was waived.

===2012–2020===
On March 1, 2012, after passing his physical exam, Dowdell signed with [[CB Gran Canaria]] in Spain.

In July 2012, Dowdell signed with [[Enisey Krasnoyarsk]] in Russia.<ref>[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/russia/41591/zabian-dowdell-inks-with-enisey.html Zabian Dowdell inks with Enisey]</ref>

On December 3, 2013, he signed a contract with [[BC Lietuvos rytas|Lietuvos Rytas]].<ref>{{cite web|title=LIETUVOS RYTAS tabs Dowdell|url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2013-14-signings/i/125113/8177/lietuvos-rytas-tabs-dowdell|website=euroleague.net|access-date=19 August 2014}}</ref> Over three [[2013–14 Euroleague|Euroleague]] games, he averaged 12 points, 3 assists and 2.7 rebounds per game.

On August 19, 2014, Dowdell signed a contract with the Belgian team [[Spirou Charleroi]].<ref>{{cite news|title=EN ATTENDANT ZABIAN DOWDELL|url=http://belgacomspirou.sudinfo.be/news/en-attendant-zabian-dowdell|access-date=19 August 2014|work=belgacomspirou.be|language=fr|archive-date=August 21, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140821030831/http://belgacomspirou.sudinfo.be/news/en-attendant-zabian-dowdell|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On July 16, 2015, he signed a one-year contract with the Russian club [[B.C. Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit Saint Petersburg]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Zenit has new point guard in Dowdell|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/67fv3oqqbo3y3gkw/zenit-has-new-point-guard-in-dowdell|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150720181155/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/67fv3oqqbo3y3gkw/zenit-has-new-point-guard-in-dowdell|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 20, 2015|access-date=July 16, 2015|work=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=July 16, 2015}}</ref>

On August 28, 2016, Dowdell signed with Italian club [[Pallacanestro Cantù]] for the 2016–17 season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/210625/cantu-signs-dowdell-and-pilepic.html Cantù signs Dowdell and Pilepic]</ref>

On November 28, 2018, he signed with [[Champagne Châlons-Reims Basket]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bebasket.fr/championnat-jeep-elite/chalons-reims-fait-revenir-zabian-dowdell-en-france.html|title=CHÂLONS-REIMS FAIT REVENIR ZABIAN DOWDELL EN FRANCE|date=November 26, 2018|publisher=BeBasket|language=fr|access-date=May 2, 2019|archive-date=May 2, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190502121957/https://www.bebasket.fr/championnat-jeep-elite/chalons-reims-fait-revenir-zabian-dowdell-en-france.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On July 25, 2019, he signed with [[Pistoia Basket 2000|Pistoia]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/oriora-pistoia-announces-zabian-dowdell/|title=OriOra Pistoia announces Zabian Dowdell|date=July 28, 2019|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=September 20, 2019|archive-date=July 25, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190725162019/https://sportando.basketball/en/oriora-pistoia-announces-zabian-dowdell/|url-status=dead}}</ref> But, before the end of the season, the team decided to replace him with the new hire [[Randy Culpepper]] and, because the number of foreign players exceeded the limit, Dowdell transferred in [[Basketball Bundesliga|Germany]] to [[Rasta Vechta]].<ref>{{cite web |title=L'OriOra Pistoia saluta Zabian Dowdell |date=28 February 2020 |url=https://www.pistoiabasket2000.com/news/prima-squadra/loriora-pistoia-saluta-zabian-dowdell/ |publisher=pistoiabasket2000.com |language=it |access-date=February 28, 2020 |archive-date=February 28, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200228201354/https://www.pistoiabasket2000.com/news/prima-squadra/loriora-pistoia-saluta-zabian-dowdell/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=REAKTION AUF YOUNG-VERLETZUNG: RASTA HOLT DOWDELL! |url=https://www.rasta-vechta.de/home/einzelansicht/reaktion-auf-young-verletzung-rasta-holt-dowdell/ |publisher=rasta-vechta.de |language=de }}</ref>
